title: Canonical ordinary and logarithmic differential square
statement:
Let Z,W,S be arbitrary schemes [def-pc-scheme], L,M,N etale log structures, and c:(Z,L)->(W,M), g:(W,M)->(S,N) log maps. Use their canonical composition [def-per-log-map-composition] and actual sheafified differential symbol quotients [def-per-log-differential-symbol-sheaf]. There exist ordinary differential presentations ΩW for g and ΩZ for gc, and tensor pullback presentations A=c*ΩW and C=c*ω_g, all with the full universal properties and the tensor-sections comparison in [def-per-etale-differential-pullback-presentation]. There exist module-sheaf maps u:A->ΩZ, v:A->C, j:ΩZ->ω_gc, iota:C->ω_gc with the following formulas on every relative etale diagram U over W, V over Z, k:V->U over c:
u(1 tensor da)=d(k-sharp a), v(1 tensor da)=1 tensor d_g a,
j(d a)=d_gc a, iota(1 tensor d_g a)=d_gc(k-sharp a),
iota(1 tensor dlog_g m)=dlog_gc(c-flat m).
They satisfy u followed by j = v followed by iota. In addition, for every module sheaf T over O_Z [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], two maps a,b:C->T are equal if they agree on every 1 tensor d_g x and every 1 tensor dlog_g m in every such relative etale diagram. No fineness, strictness, smoothness, saturation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Construct the ordinary etale differential presentations by the ordinary relative differential sheaf and universal derivation, transported to its tensor sections on etale objects. On affine etale charts, etaleness identifies the pullback of ordinary relative differentials with the relative differentials on the chart. The universal derivations and their universal maps commute with restrictions and glue. This gives both ordinary presentations with their full universal properties and normalized tensor-sections comparisons.
Construct A and C by inverse image followed by extension of scalars and module sheafification. The tensor adjunction yields the relative-section units and the stated universal properties.

proof.text: The ordinary universal derivation on Z gives u. The ordinary symbols in ω_g and ω_gc give v and j. Pullback of the ordinary and log symbols along c preserves the six defining relations, including both base relations, so the free-symbol map descends to the quotient, sheafification and tensor extension to give iota. These constructions give all five formulas. On 1 tensor da both u followed by j and v followed by iota are d_gc(k-sharp a); ordinary and tensor universality imply commutativity.

For a,b:C->T use the tensor adjunction to regard their composites with the unit as semilinear relative-section maps from ω_g. Agreement on ordinary and log symbols gives agreement on the free symbol presheaf. Since both maps already kill the relations, they agree on the cokernel; the sheafification adjunction then gives equality on the differential sheaf. The tensor universal property gives a=b. The sheaf argument applies on all relative diagrams; it does not assert that global symbols span each section module without taking a cover.

lean.statement:
theorem logDifferential_canonical_square {Z W S : Scheme.{u}}
    {L : EtaleLogStructure Z} {M : EtaleLogStructure W} {N : EtaleLogStructure S}
    (c : EtaleLogMap L M) (g : EtaleLogMap M N) :
    ∃ (ΩW : EtaleOrdinaryDifferentialPresentation g.base)
      (ΩZ : EtaleOrdinaryDifferentialPresentation (c.base ≫ g.base))
      (A : EtaleDifferentialPullbackPresentation c.base ΩW.module)
      (C : EtaleDifferentialPullbackPresentation c.base g.differentialSheaf)
      (u : A.module ⟶ ΩZ.module) (v : A.module ⟶ C.module)
      (j : ΩZ.module ⟶ (c.comp g).differentialSheaf)
      (iota : C.module ⟶ (c.comp g).differentialSheaf),
      (∀ (U : W.Etale) (V : Z.Etale) (k : V.left ⟶ U.left)
        (hk : k ≫ U.hom = V.hom ≫ c.base) (a : Γ(U.left, ⊤)),
        u.val.app (op V) (A.unit.app U V k hk (ΩW.derivation.d (X := op U) a)) =
          ΩZ.derivation.d (X := op V) (k.appTop a)) ∧
      (∀ (U : W.Etale) (V : Z.Etale) (k : V.left ⟶ U.left)
        (hk : k ≫ U.hom = V.hom ≫ c.base) (a : Γ(U.left, ⊤)),
        v.val.app (op V) (A.unit.app U V k hk (ΩW.derivation.d (X := op U) a)) =
          C.unit.app U V k hk (g.sheafD U a)) ∧
      (∀ (V : Z.Etale) (a : Γ(V.left, ⊤)),
        j.val.app (op V) (ΩZ.derivation.d (X := op V) a) = (c.comp g).sheafD V a) ∧
      (∀ (U : W.Etale) (V : Z.Etale) (k : V.left ⟶ U.left)
        (hk : k ≫ U.hom = V.hom ≫ c.base) (a : Γ(U.left, ⊤)),
        iota.val.app (op V) (C.unit.app U V k hk (g.sheafD U a)) =
          (c.comp g).sheafD V (k.appTop a)) ∧
      (∀ (U : W.Etale) (V : Z.Etale) (k : V.left ⟶ U.left)
        (hk : k ≫ U.hom = V.hom ≫ c.base) (m : M.monoidSheaf.obj.obj (op U)),
        iota.val.app (op V) (C.unit.app U V k hk (g.sheafDLog U m)) =
          (c.comp g).sheafDLog V (c.sectionMap U V k hk m)) ∧
      u ≫ j = v ≫ iota ∧
      (∀ (T : DifferentialEtaleModules Z) (a b : C.module ⟶ T),
        (∀ (U : W.Etale) (V : Z.Etale) (k : V.left ⟶ U.left)
          (hk : k ≫ U.hom = V.hom ≫ c.base) (x : Γ(U.left, ⊤)),
          a.val.app (op V) (C.unit.app U V k hk (g.sheafD U x)) =
            b.val.app (op V) (C.unit.app U V k hk (g.sheafD U x))) →
        (∀ (U : W.Etale) (V : Z.Etale) (k : V.left ⟶ U.left)
          (hk : k ≫ U.hom = V.hom ≫ c.base) (m : M.monoidSheaf.obj.obj (op U)),
          a.val.app (op V) (C.unit.app U V k hk (g.sheafDLog U m)) =
            b.val.app (op V) (C.unit.app U V k hk (g.sheafDLog U m))) → a = b)
